In this video, we explore Laya, a multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision model designed for fast classification, scoring, and structured decision-making. [...] Instead of generating text and then parsing it into JSON or another structured format, Laya takes a state such as text, email, ticket, or JSON along with typed questions, and returns structured answers with probabilities in a single forward pass. In this video, we cover: [...] The demo shows how Laya can be used for practical decision tasks such as department routing, urgency detection, churn-risk assessment, and identifying refund requests. title: Jev Engineering: how to build the fastest AI Agent Brain in 10 Steps (Full-Setup) | Movez (@0xMovez) on X
snippet: Sep 17 Yeah Jev by @typesafeai is very cool. It classified 500 emails in seconds. And it costed 3.5 cents. 00:00 125 @CompleteSkeptic Diogo Almeida TypeSafe AI @CompleteSkeptic Sep 15 We believe that the future is code + AI, so made workflow evals to reflect that Jev costs: $42 / BILLION input tokens ($0.042 / MTok) and output tokens are free (forever - they’re too cheap to meter with our new architecture) Jev is named after Jevons paradox and off the 52 @nutlope Hassan [...] ### Conclusion: Jev is not another chatbot. It is a fast decision layer that reads the current state of your system and chooses between the options you define. And the real alpha is not the 7-second flight demo or the $0.08 paper classification. The real alpha is realizing how many expensive LLM calls inside your agents never needed generation: Let the LLM research, plan, and write. Let Jev route, score, approve, or escalate. Let code execute the decision. [...] That job contains several decisions: Do we have enough sources? Which worker goes next? Is the draft ready for review? Those are candidates for Jev. Fetching sources, writing paragraphs, and saving files still belong to your tools and generative models. An exact rule, such as stopping after ten actions, belongs in code. The split is simple. If the operation creates text, it stays with the LLM. If the operation picks an option from a list, scores a value, or answers yes/no, it goes to Jev.

snippet: # santi on X: "¿qué es un System One model? TypeSafe usa ese nombre para modelos de IA diseñados para tomar decisiones rápidas y estructuradas. Jev es el primero. entienden lenguaje natural, pero devuelven elecciones, puntajes y probabilidades en lugar de generar texto libre. para entender cómo funcionan, hay 5 conceptos: 1) State: la información que el modelo evalúa. puede ser un mensaje, una conversación o un JSON con datos relevantes. 2) Choice: elige entre opciones que vos definís. devuelve [...] definís. devuelve la elección y la probabilidad de cada opción. 3) Score: evalúa algo sobre una escala sobre niveles que describís vos. devuelve un puntaje que puede quedar entre 2 niveles. 4) Noul: evalúa una pregunta de sí/no. devuelve la probabilidad de que la respuesta sea sí. 5) Structure: permite organizar las instrucciones y los criterios en JSON, con descripciones y ejemplos que aclaren qué evaluar. en las capturas se ve un ejemplo muy claro: un cliente tiene problemas para conectar su [...] crear un ticket para soporte técnico y marcarlo como urgente, sin que alguien tenga que leer y clasificar el mensaje a mano. \la primera imagen muestra qué le enviás. la segunda, qué devuelve."
